tour.title: Project overview: two engines, one pipeline
tour.description: Start at document:firefox/README.md for the big picture: this graph covers how Gecko turns markup bytes into a styled DOM. The README links the two halves of the story — file:firefox/parser/html/nsHtml5TreeBuilder.cpp on the HTML side and the Stylo crate under servo/components/style on the CSS side. Skim document:firefox/servo/components/style/README.md, then open file:firefox/servo/components/style/context.rs to see the StyleContext and file:firefox/servo/components/style/gecko/data.rs for the PerDocumentStyleData that hold stylesheet and stylist state. Keep in mind the tour follows two chains that meet at the end: element creation (C++) and the property pipeline (Rust).
tour.languageLesson: The codebase is a C++ host (XPCOM, ns-prefixed classes) embedding a Rust library (Stylo) — the tour will repeatedly cross that FFI boundary.

tour.title: Chain A begins: parsing markup in the tree builder
tour.description: Bytes become tags in file:firefox/parser/html/nsHtml5TreeBuilder.cpp: trace startTagElementInBody/startTagInBody and dispatchCaseSensitivity, the HTML5 state machine that decides what each start tag means. Each recognized tag name resolves through a precomputed entry in file:firefox/parser/html/nsHtml5ElementName.cpp (the element name tables carrying group flags like HTMLELEMGROUP_*). Interned names come from file:firefox/parser/html/nsHtml5AtomTable.h, keeping token names cheap to compare later. This stage emits tree-operation commands, not DOM nodes yet.
tour.languageLesson: nsHtml5TreeBuilder is C++ transpiled from Java: notice table-driven dispatch and integer group flags instead of virtual calls, a performance idiom for hot parser loops.

tour.title: From tag name to C++ object: the element factory
tour.description: When the tree builder executes a 'create element' operation it calls function:firefox/dom/html/HTMLElementFactory.cpp:CreateHTMLElement inside file:firefox/dom/html/HTMLElementFactory.cpp. Observe the tag-to-creator lookup: a static table (built with macros like HTML_ELEMENT_ROW / NS_New*Element entries) maps nsHTMLTag enums straight to constructor functions with no string comparison. The declared contract is in file:firefox/dom/base/nsContentCreatorFunctions.h (CreateHTMLElement, NewHTMLHTMLElement, etc.), which the parser and XBL/frames code both use. This is the single choke point where a tag name in a byte stream picks a concrete C++ class.
tour.languageLesson: Classic C++ technique: a function-pointer table generated by macros gives O(1) tag dispatch and lets you add an element by editing one row, not a switch statement.

tour.title: The element class hierarchy takes shape
tour.description: Every creator from step 3 returns an instance of a class derived from class:firefox/dom/html/nsGenericHTMLElement.h:nsGenericHTMLElement, the shared base holding tag parsing helpers (ParseAttribute, MapNoneAttributesInto) and style-relevant plumbing. Compare a concrete leaf like file:firefox/dom/html/HTMLAnchorElement.cpp (href handling, link color state) with file:firefox/dom/html/HTMLElement.cpp for the generic <html> element. All of them ultimately derive from class:firefox/dom/base/Element.h:Element, the abstract gateway to the style system via GetComputedStyle and inline-style declarations. Note the ctor chain each element runs through — this is Chain A's spine.
tour.languageLesson: Gecko uses deep multiple inheritance (nsGenericHTMLElement -> nsHTMLElement -> Element -> FragmentOrElement -> nsINode) with XPCOM interfaces (NS_DECL_ISUPPORTS); virtual dtors and refcounted AddRef/Release manage object lifetime.

tour.title: Node identity: nsINode, FragmentOrElement, and NodeInfo
tour.description: Follow the base-ctor chain down: file:firefox/dom/base/FragmentOrElement.cpp implements child-list and shadow-DOM machinery, and file:firefox/dom/base/nsINode.h defines the root node interface (GetParentElement, OwnerDoc, node type constants). Identity is not the C++ pointer but the NodeInfo from file:firefox/dom/base/nsNodeInfoManager.cpp — a shared, interned (tag name, namespace) record that makes two <a> nodes comparable by NodeInfo pointer and feeds selector matching later. Observe how constructor arguments thread a nsNodeInfoManager into every nsINode. With the element fully built and attached, Chain A hands off to styling.
tour.languageLesson: Flyweight pattern via shared nsINodeInfo objects: interning identity data saves memory per node and turns namespace/tag comparisons into pointer equality.

tour.title: Chain B begins: CSS properties are data, then code
tour.description: Switch to the style side: every CSS longhand is declared as a TOML table in config:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/longhands.toml (name, Rust type, initial value, style struct) and config:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/shorthands.toml (expansion kinds like four_sides). file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/data.py parses these into Property objects, and file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/build.py drives Mako to render file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/properties.mako.rs — thousands of lines of parse/cascade/computed-value Rust code that no human maintains. Understanding this file explains where functions like longhands::margin::parse_declared actually come from.
tour.languageLesson: Codegen pipeline (TOML + Python + Mako templates emitting Rust) keeps ~500 properties consistent at compile time — the Rust code reads as if hand-written but regenerates from spec data.

tour.title: Loading and parsing a stylesheet
tour.description: A web page's CSS arrives via file:firefox/layout/style/Loader.cpp (Loader::LoadStyleSheet), which wraps results in file:firefox/layout/style/StyleSheet.h — the C++ half of the shared StyleSheet object also owned by Rust. Parsing itself happens inside Stylo: file:firefox/servo/components/style/selector_parser.rs turns selector text into typed Selector structs, including Gecko-specific pseudo-classes. The C++ view of the resulting rule list is file:firefox/layout/style/ServoCSSRuleList.cpp, which lazily bridges rule indices back to Rust. Note that both languages see the same rules through the shared lock, so mutation is safe across FFI.
tour.languageLesson: SharedRwLock (shared_lock.rs) guards data owned across the FFI: the same lock type is exposed to C++ and Rust so neither side can race the other on stylesheet mutation.

tour.title: The Stylist indexes rules for fast matching
tour.description: Parsed rules are registered into file:firefox/servo/components/style/stylist.rs (Stylist::push_applicable_author_style / update), the per-document machine that owns one file:firefox/servo/components/style/selector_map.rs (SelectorMap) per cascade origin and pseudo-element. Observe how SelectorMap buckets selectors by the rightmost simple selector (id, class, local-name) via its hash maps — this is what makes matching sublinear. file:firefox/servo/components/style/stylesheet_set.rs tracks which sheets are dirty so invalidation only rebuilds what changed. After this step, every rule has a precomputed index entry keyed by what an element could match.
tour.languageLesson: Rust generics + closures shine here: SelectorMap is generic over Impl (the selector trait impl), letting Servo and Gecko reuse the same container with different pseudo-class types.

tour.title: Selector matching collects candidate rules
tour.description: Styling one element starts in file:firefox/servo/components/style/matching.rs (match_element), which drives file:firefox/servo/components/style/rule_collector.rs to walk the SelectorMap buckets for each origin (UA, user, author) and run the Bloom-filtered ancestor check from bloom.rs concepts. Collected declarations are then pushed into the rule tree: file:firefox/servo/components/style/rule_tree/core.rs implements the lexicographic-ish tree shared by all elements, and file:firefox/servo/components/style/rule_tree/level.rs defines the Level enum (Author, User, UA, important variants) that orders specificity. Trace RuleCollector::collect to see hints become RuleNodes — the deduplicated path that cascade will read.
tour.languageLesson: The rule tree is a DAG of declarations with interior mutability and unsafe raw pointers (rule_tree/unsafe_box.rs) for lock-free sharing — a deliberate Rust-unsafe island behind a safe API.

tour.title: Cascade: resolving declarations to computed values
tour.description: Now the Element's style context flows through file:firefox/servo/components/style/style_resolver.rs (StyleResolver::resolve_style), which pulls the rule node path from the rule tree and hands declared values to file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/cascade.rs (cascade_and_compute, apply_declarations). That generated function walks every property in cascade order, applying importance, animation, and inheritance rules — the per-property code lives in file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/mod.rs from step 6's codegen. Finally file:firefox/servo/components/style/style_adjuster.rs applies Gecko adjustments (blockification, display fixes). Output: one ComputedValues with every longhand resolved.
tour.languageLesson: Cascade is macro/loop-generated per property: Rust closures (PropertyDeclarationApplication) plus generated match arms give virtual-dispatch-like behavior with zero dyn overhead.

tour.title: The FFI bridge: ComputedValues becomes nsStyleStructs
tour.description: Computed values must reach C++ layout: file:firefox/servo/components/style/properties/gecko.mako.rs (another Mako output) contains the setgecko / copygecko code that copies each Rust value into the Gecko nsStyle* C structs, e.g. Gecko_StyleMarginSetFromComputedStyle. The call crosses file:firefox/servo/components/style/gecko_bindings/bindings.rs (bindgen-generated extern fns) into file:firefox/layout/style/GeckoBindings.cpp, the hand-written C++ shim that writes into the structs declared in file:firefox/layout/style/nsStyleStruct.h (nsStyleMargin, nsStyleDisplay, nsStyleText...). The C++ side orchestrates all of this from class:firefox/layout/style/ServoStyleSet.h:ServoStyleSet, Gecko's handle to the Stylo engine.
tour.languageLesson: FFI discipline: repr(C) structs on the Rust side mirror C++ layout, bindgen generates the extern declarations, and every unsafe call site assumes the other language upholds invariants (null-ness, borrowing).

tour.title: Where the chains meet: an element's computed style, exposed to JS
tour.description: Chain A built the Element; Chain B filled its ComputedValues; they meet when layout or script asks for style: file:firefox/servo/components/style/gecko/wrapper.rs is the TElement/TNode view that let Stylo walk the C++ DOM during matching in the first place, and class:firefox/layout/style/ServoStyleSet.h:ServoStyleSet drove the traversal (ServoStyleSet::StyleDocument). To see the result from script, trace function:firefox/layout/style/nsComputedDOMStyle.cpp:nsComputedDOMStyle::GetPropertyValue in file:firefox/layout/style/nsComputedDOMStyle.cpp — it maps a CSS property name onto the right nsStyleStruct field (via getters in nsStyleStructInlines.h / nsCSSProps.cpp lookups) and formats it as an nsDOMCSSDeclaration string. That call is the public end of the entire pipeline you just followed.
tour.languageLesson: Getter caching in nsComputedDOMStyle shows a C++ idiom: mDirty flags plus lazy computation of derived values (GetAbsoluteOffset, GetMarginWidth) so getComputedStyle only pays for what script reads.

tour.title: The built-in stylesheets every document gets
tour.description: Firefox ships its default CSS as built-in UA stylesheets: html.css defines per-element defaults, ua.css styles anonymous boxes, forms.css the form controls, counterstyles.css the predefined @counter-style rules. file:firefox/layout/style/GlobalStyleSheetCache.cpp loads them all at startup and hands them to the style set, so they participate in the cascade before any author CSS.
tour.languageLesson: Declarative resources shipped as data: UA behavior that other engines hard-code in C++ is mostly ordinary CSS files here, loaded through the same cascade as page styles.

tour.title: CSSOM: every rule type has a C++ twin
tour.description: Each CSS at-rule is exposed to script through a C++ wrapper — CSSStyleRule, CSSMediaRule, CSSFontFaceRule, CSSImportRule... — that holds the raw Stylo rule and forwards accessors over Servo_* FFI. css::Rule is the shared base; GroupRule/ConditionRule cover nesting. Trace file:firefox/layout/style/CSSStyleRule.cpp to see declaration mutation flow back into Stylo.
tour.languageLesson: Thin-wrapper pattern: C++ owns lifetime and WebIDL surface; all parsing/serialization semantics stay in Rust, one FFI call per accessor.

tour.title: Restyle: how a DOM change becomes new style
tour.description: When script mutates the DOM, file:firefox/layout/style/RestyleManager.cpp records element snapshots, posts restyle hints, and drives ServoStyleSet::StyleDocument — the Servo traversal that recomputes only what is dirty. Its post-traversal turns style differences into change hints that reconstruct or repaint frames.
tour.languageLesson: Invalidation-first architecture: the C++ side decides WHAT is dirty; the Rust traversal decides the new values; the post-traversal converts diffs into layout work.

tour.title: CSS Typed OM: values as objects
tour.description: getComputedStyle-like strings are not the only API: layout/style/typedom implements CSSStyleValue and its subclasses (CSSKeywordValue, CSSUnitValue, CSSTransformValue...). CSSStyleValue::ParseStyleValue calls Servo_DeclarationBlock_Parse and maps the returned typed value tag onto a C++ subclass, backed by Stylo's typed_om module.
tour.languageLesson: Tagged-union bridging: one Rust enum (StyleValueType) fans out into a C++ class hierarchy via factory dispatch.

tour.title: Inside the HTML5 parser: bytes to createElement
tour.description: The full parse chain: nsHtml5Tokenizer tokenizes bytes into tags, nsHtml5ElementName resolves tag names via generated tables, and nsHtml5TreeBuilder runs the HTML5 tree-construction state machine. Tree operations are queued and executed by nsHtml5TreeOpExecutor, which reaches HTMLElementFactory::CreateHTMLElement — where Chain A of the tour began. With Stage 3, every intermediate file of that chain is now a first-class node.
tour.languageLesson: nsHtml5 is machine-translated from Java: table-driven state machines, no virtual dispatch in hot loops, and UTF-16 throughout — the same design the Java validator htmlparser uses.

tour.title: The chain boundary: frames build the display list
tour.description: This is where both chains terminate. nsCSSFrameConstructor reads the computed style (display, etc.) to construct the right frame for each element; frames implement BuildDisplayList, appending display items — nsDisplayBackgroundImage, nsDisplayBorder, nsDisplayText — that directly read the nsStyle* structs the cascade produced. Beyond this boundary lies painting and compositing, which the call-graph database deliberately treats as out of scope.
tour.languageLesson: Gecko separates style (what values), layout (what frames), and painting (what pixels): the display list is the hand-off point — a retained, sorted list of paint commands derived from frames and their computed styles.
